caption:
5 Bali beaches most people walk right past.

05 Suluban: you duck under the cliff to get in
04 Gunung Payung: 280 steps, or the shuttle
03 Green Bowl: look down at low tide
02 Nyang Nyang: 1.5 km of sand, a few footprints
01 Impossibles: only there when the tide allows

Save this for your trip, and check the tide before you go. Number 1 is four minutes' walk from Yume by Nyara, our three private-pool villas above Bingin. Link in bio to book your stay in Bali.

slides.sub: Number 1 is four minutes from our gate. Guess it before you get there.
slides.credit: Uluwatu. Photo: Zexsen Xie, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Suluban means “to pass under”. Walk down to Uluwatu Beach, then duck through the gap in the rock. Go at low tide: high water fills the cave.
slides.credit: Suluban. Photo: I Made Jon Arinata, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.answer: Yes. Or ride the shuttle down.
slides.body: A white-sand cove on the south coast, named for the clifftop temple above it. Shade in the caves at the back, and quieter than its famous neighbour, Pandawa.
slides.credit: Gunung Payung. Photo: Yosep Sasada, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: About 300 steps lead to a 60-metre cove where the reef forms a green bowl. Caves at the back give shade. Watch your bag up top: the monkeys are quick.
slides.credit: Green Bowl. Photo: Vladimir E, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.answer: 1.5 km of sand. A few footprints.
slides.body: Around 500 steps down on Bali's southern tip, with an old shipwreck at the far end. No lifeguards here, so read the water before you swim.
slides.credit: Nyang Nyang. Photo: Schweigeblick, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Between Bingin and Padang Padang, the sand only shows at low tide. Check a tide chart, then take the cliff path down. Yume sits four minutes' walk above it.
slides.credit: Above Impossibles: Yume by Nyara, Bingin

slides.eyebrow: NOW YOU KNOW WHERE TO SWIM
